title: a remote URL carrying a token reaches the terminal and the release log whole when release_repo cannot read OWNER/NAME from it: its refusal prints the configured URL, credentials and all
body:
## Problem

`release_repo` (lib/release.steps:637) reads the repository off the remote's configured URL when `release.repo` is not declared. When the URL names no host (:673), or its path is not OWNER/NAME (:680), it refuses with a warning that prints the URL as configured: `remote origin's url (<url>) is not HOST/OWNER/NAME -- declare release.repo: OWNER/NAME`. A URL that carries credentials, `https://user:<token>@host/group/sub/repo.git` or the scp form `<token>@host:group/sub/repo`, as a GitLab subgroup or an Azure DevOps path gives, is printed whole, token included. The success path strips the userinfo (`rest="${rest#*@}"`) and prints only OWNER/NAME or HOST/OWNER/NAME, so a token is exposed only on the refusals.

The refusal reaches the terminal, the release's sealed log under tmp/release/, and in CI the job's log. Its callers are lib/cmd/release:425, :764 (step 6's FAILED row, through cut_fail), :1086 and lib/release.steps:721.

Found by critic-shell reviewing 0187 (cc, 2026-10-08).

## Measured (vc, 2026-10-08, main 674a7608)

In a scratch repository, `release_repo "" ""` with `origin` at:

- `https://user:FAKE-TOKEN-0188@gitlab.example/group/sub/repo.git`: rc 1, and the warning carries the URL whole, `user:FAKE-TOKEN-0188` included.
- `https://user:FAKE-TOKEN-0188@github.com/owner/name.git`: rc 0, `owner/name`, no token.
- `https://gitlab.example/group/sub/repo.git`, the control: rc 1, the same warning, nothing secret in it.

Not driven: the `names no host` refusal (:673), which prints the URL the same way.

## Fix

Neither refusal prints a URL's userinfo. It names the remote and what was read from it with the credentials left out, eg the URL with its userinfo removed, or the host and path alone, through one helper, so the two warnings cannot differ. Each refusal still names the remote and says to declare `release.repo: OWNER/NAME`.

## Done when

1. With a token in the remote URL and a path that is not OWNER/NAME, in the URL form and the scp form, the refusal carries neither the token nor the user, red on main first, and still names the remote and the remedy.
2. The `names no host` refusal prints no userinfo either, driven with a URL that reaches it carrying credentials, or the Resolution shows that no such URL reaches it.
3. A URL with no credentials reads as before in both refusals, and the OWNER/NAME success path is unchanged: the controls.

## Resolution

Landed at 7263bc00 on a green full suite (vc's, 2273 of 2273 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261008-0906).

1. `release_url_shown <url>`, in lib/release.steps beside `release_repo`, is what a message may print of a url: the url with its userinfo left out. The userinfo is everything before the last @ ahead of the first `/`, so a password holding a raw @ is left out whole. With a scheme the search starts after its `://`, and an @ in the path is kept. With none, as in the scp form, it starts at the url's first byte and runs past the `:` where an scp path begins, which catches a password ahead of a host with no `:` after it.
2. Both of `release_repo`'s refusals print the url through it, so the two cannot differ: `remote origin's url (https://gitlab.example/group/sub/repo.git) is not HOST/OWNER/NAME -- declare release.repo: OWNER/NAME`, and the same for `names no host`. Each still names the remote and the remedy. The refusal reaches the terminal, a cut's sealed log under tmp/release/ and CI's job log, through pre-flight's gh check, step 6's object read, status's row 9 and the object's content read; it carries no userinfo on any of them.
3. A host holding an @ is refused: `remote origin's url (...) holds more than one @ ahead of its host, so where its userinfo ends cannot be told -- write an @ in a userinfo as %40, or declare release.repo: OWNER/NAME`. Such a url held more than one @ ahead of its host, and the success path, which reads the userinfo to the first @, made the rest of the password the host. With an OWNER/NAME path, gh was told that host in `--repo`, and pre-flight asked gh whether it was signed in there and printed it. Refused, no url `release_repo` accepts can be read two ways: where it reads to the first @ and the helper to the last, the two now agree.
4. A url with no userinfo reads as before in both refusals, and the success path, which reads OWNER/NAME past a userinfo, is unchanged for every url it accepted but one whose host held an @.
5. docs/configuration.md says that where the remote's url is why a repository cannot be resolved, the row names that url with its userinfo left out; that a url holding more than one @ ahead of its host is refused; what is printed regardless; and, in pre-flight's list, that the repository must resolve for gh to be asked about its host.

Done when 2: a url with no scheme and no `:` after its @, such as `user:token@host/group/repo`, reaches the names-no-host refusal, and an arm drives one.

The arms, all six carrying 0188 in their titles:

- In releasestatus.bats, the not-HOST/OWNER/NAME refusal, in the URL form, the scp form and with glob characters in the token: row 9 names the url without its userinfo, and neither the token nor the user is in the output. Every shape is read before the arm fails, so its failure names each one that printed userinfo.
- The names-no-host refusal, the same, with a token and a user in a url with no scheme.
- A url holding more than one @ ahead of its host, in the URL form with a path that is not OWNER/NAME, the URL form on github.com with an OWNER/NAME path, and the scp form with an OWNER/NAME path: row 9 refuses each, naming the url without its userinfo, the output carries none of it, and gh is never told it.
- The controls: a plain url and one with an @ in its path, each refused as not HOST/OWNER/NAME, and a plain url with no host, each named as configured; and OWNER/NAME read past a token, where gh is told the repository. Nothing on that path prints the url, so its refutes are guards, and `repo_told` is its red.
- In releasecut.bats, a cut refused at pre-flight for a url that is not HOST/OWNER/NAME: the terminal and the cut's sealed log both carry the refusal, and neither carries the userinfo. The sealed log is the terminal stream teed, so its scan is a guard, and with the terminal's three assertions removed it goes red alone on main's code.
- A cut whose url holds more than one @ ahead of its host is refused at pre-flight: gh is never asked about the password, and neither the terminal nor the sealed log carries it.

`origin_at`, a new fixture in tests/lib/release_fixtures.bash, the one home both files load, sets origin's configured url while insteadOf sends every git read of it to the bare remote, so nothing reaches the network. The url-shape arm uses it too.

Evidence, in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/0188/runs/. The build is 72abff10 in a scratch clone: main's code once batch 4 landed (main 476cf82e with cc's 0186 v1.1 and 0187 v1.1), then 0181 v1.1 (184b28f9), then 0188. The runs below are on its twin c9465a87, the same five commits on 0181 v1 (95dbeef7), which differs from 72abff10 only in releasecut.bats's header comment, 0181 v1.1's one change.

- Red on main 476cf82e first, the build's arm files and the two test libraries they load copied in, under BSD tools and with GNU tools first on PATH (red-476cf82e-{bsd,gnu}-20261008-084414.log): five arms red and the control green, the same under both, no helper missing. Each red arm fails where it aims. The first names each of its shapes, printing its userinfo in row 9 and in the output; the names-no-host arm fails at row 9; the arm for more than one @ names each of its shapes, two of them with gh told `--repo TOKEN-0188@github.com/t/demo` and `--repo FAKE-TOKEN-0188@gitlab.example/group/repo`; the first cut fails at the url its refusal names; and the second at gh asked `auth status --hostname TOKEN-0188@gitlab.example`.
- Mutants, 11, each applied once and parsed, run on the twin with the fix and the base, 0181 v1's release library, under both tool sets: 26 of 26 sections as aimed (var-20261008-085139/), no arm red beyond its aim, and each mutant's failure lines read against the assertion it aims at, the same under both. The mutants: the helper printing the url as configured; reading to the first @, which only the urls with more than one @ catch; reading to the last @ anywhere, its path included, which only the control's @ in a path catches; a url with a scheme read as though it had none; the scheme left out, which the second cut catches at the url its refusal names, past its refutes; the userinfo read as a pattern, which only the token with glob characters catches; each refusal in turn printing the url as configured; the password left out and the user kept, which the second cut catches at its user's refute, past its token's; and the host refusal dropped, and printing the url as configured. The base fails as main does.
- `release_url_shown` driven directly over 15 urls: the URL and scp forms, a user with no password, a raw @ in the password, an @ in the path and in a query, a token holding glob characters, no path, `file://`, a plain path, `user@host` and the empty url.
- shellcheck 0.11.0 is clean on lib/release.steps, and a planted defect in a control file fails it. 0187's credentials pattern finds nothing in lib/release.steps, and finds the shape planted in a control line.
- The targeted run (releasestatus, releasecut, releasecore and release, with helpers, contract, neutral, documentation, readonlygit, harness and help), on the twin c9465a87 with its tree clean before and after: under BSD tools 535 of 535 (targeted-bsd-20261008-085419.log, 08:54:19Z to 09:06:47Z), and with GNU tools first on PATH 535 of 535 (targeted-gnu-20261008-090647.log, 09:06:47Z to 09:20:22Z). Two in each are harness.bats arms whose subject is `require_command`'s own skip, and they skip as they expect. neutral.bats carries 0187's credentials arm, so it reads lib/release.steps' new comments too.
- The patch is `git diff` from 0181 v1.1's head, 184b28f9, to 72abff10: 5 files, 210 insertions and 7 deletions. It applies clean on a fresh clone of main 28a2a161 after 0181 v1.1's patch, batch 5's order. Every one of its five files is then 72abff10's bytes, and outside intent/ that tree is the build's.
- critic-shell reviewed the build and found no critical, four warnings and three recommendations, all folded: the host refusal, so the success path and the helper cannot disagree on a url either accepts; `origin_at` in the fixtures' one home; the comments and the docs saying, per form, what the helper leaves out and what it cannot; the arm comments narrowed to the output `release_repo` makes; the guard in the first cut arm driven red alone; and the github.com url with more than one @, which the success path had read with the password in its host.

Declared limits:

- In the scp form, an @ inside the path's first segment, as in `git@host:team@x/repo`, ends the userinfo, so a refusal leaves the host out too. Nothing secret is printed.
- The helper prints a raw `/` in a userinfo whole, by design: its search for the userinfo stops at the first `/`, so that an @ in a path is never read as the end of one, and git cannot read such a url either. It also reads a `://` anywhere as the scheme's, and does not look for a secret elsewhere in a url, such as a query parameter.
- git's and ssh's own messages, which pre-flight's UNREADABLE row and step 8's pushes print as they come, are not rewritten here, and ssh's refusal names its user. The arms cannot see them, since insteadOf hands git the bare remote's path. docs/configuration.md says they are not rewritten; issue 0189 takes them on, sharing `release_url_shown`, and changing that sentence is 0189's.
